name: dev.aicomputeradar/ai-compute-radar
title: AI Compute Radar
description: Which open models fit your GPU or Mac, measured. Model momentum, GPU rental prices, weekly pick.

tools.name: trending_models
tools.description: Tracked AI models ranked by Heat Score (0–100, weighted percentiles of measured Hugging Face/OpenRouter signals) with the raw signals, local-run facts (GGUF size, quantization) and links. Models still collecting a week of history have heat=null and rank after scored ones.

slug.description: Return a single model by slug.

tools.name: find_fit
tools.description: Which tracked models run on a given GPU or Mac: measured GGUF weights + computed context cache + runtime overhead versus usable memory. Returns the best recommendation and every verdict (EXCELLENT/GOOD/TIGHT/OFFLOAD_REQUIRED/NOT_RECOMMENDED/UNKNOWN) with plain-language reasons, plus summary counts over all tracked models. For a short answer pass show "fits" (only models that run fully on the machine), a limit, or compact true (one row per model: name, quantization, verdict, total GB). The machine is a hardware id from list_hardware, several identical cards (count), or, for a machine that is not listed, a free memory figure (memory_gb, with type "mac" for unified memory); what a machine off the list assumes is said in hardware.assumptions.

hardware.description: Hardware id or page slug, e.g. rtx-4090, mac-studio-m3-ultra-96gb. Leave it out when you pass memory_gb.

count.description: How many identical graphics cards (default 1). Their memory adds up; the answer says what that assumes.

memory_gb.description: For a machine that is not on the list, instead of hardware: the memory of one graphics card, or of the Mac, in GB.

type.description: What memory_gb describes: "gpu" (default, a plug-in card) or "mac" (unified memory).

ram_gb.description: System RAM behind the card(s), for what spills over (default 32).

show.description: Which verdicts to list: all (default), fits (runs fully on the machine), fits_or_spills (also those that spill into system RAM).

limit.description: At most this many rows, best first.

compact.description: One short row per model instead of the full arithmetic and reasons.

tools.name: best_quant
tools.description: Which file of a model to download for a machine. Every GGUF quantization the repo publishes is read from its file listing (sizes measured, split files summed), the memory each needs at your context length is computed, and the answer names the largest file that runs on the machine with room (pick), a larger one that only barely fits (stretch), when nothing runs at that context the file that runs at the longest shorter one (atShorterContext), and for every file its verdict, its bits per weight and the longest context it still runs at. Works for a tracked model (model, a slug) and for any public Hugging Face repo (repo). The machine is a hardware id, several identical cards (count), or a free memory figure (memory_gb). Files are ranked by size only: a larger file keeps more bits per weight; there is no quality rating and no speed figure. When the model's shape cannot be read every verdict is UNKNOWN and only the sizes are given. Limits as for measure_model: 20 calls per hour per caller; a reading is reused for 24 hours.

model.description: A tracked model by slug, e.g. qwen3-8b. Slugs come from trending_models. Pass this or repo, not both.

repo.description: Any public Hugging Face repo as "owner/name" (a GGUF repo, or an original whose most downloaded GGUF build is then used), or its huggingface.co link.

hardware.description: Hardware id, e.g. rtx-3060-12gb. Ids come from list_hardware. Leave it out when you pass memory_gb.

count.description: How many identical graphics cards (default 1). Their memory adds up; the answer says what that assumes.

memory_gb.description: For a machine that is not on the list, instead of hardware: the memory of one graphics card, or of the Mac, in GB.

type.description: What memory_gb describes: "gpu" (default, a plug-in card) or "mac" (unified memory).

ram_gb.description: System RAM behind the card(s), for what spills over (default 32).

context.description: Context length in tokens (default 8192); capped at the model's own window.

tools.name: measure_model
tools.description: Beta, for models that are not on the tracked list. Give any public Hugging Face repo: the 4-bit GGUF file is read from its file listing (or from its most downloaded GGUF build), and the answer gives the memory the model needs and the fit verdict per machine. File size is measured, the context cache is computed from the config of the repo or of the model it was made from, the runtime share is an assumption. When the shape cannot be read the verdict is UNKNOWN and only the file size is given. No speed figures. Limits: 20 calls per hour per caller, 40 new repos per hour in all; a reading is reused for 24 hours. For tracked models find_fit has no such limit.

repo.description: The repo as "owner/name", e.g. TheDrummer/Cydonia-24B-v4.1, or its huggingface.co link.

hardware.description: One hardware id, e.g. rtx-3060-12gb. Without it (and without memory_gb) the verdict is given for every machine on the list.

count.description: How many identical graphics cards (default 1). Their memory adds up; the answer says what that assumes.

memory_gb.description: For a machine that is not on the list, instead of hardware: the memory of one graphics card, or of the Mac, in GB.

type.description: What memory_gb describes: "gpu" (default, a plug-in card) or "mac" (unified memory).

ram_gb.description: System RAM behind the card(s), for what spills over (default 32).

context.description: Context length in tokens (default 8192); capped at the model's own window.

tools.name: community_versions
tools.description: The most downloaded versions of tracked open language models that other people made (finetunes, abliterated or pruned variants, merges), each measured: maker, the tracked model it comes from, the GGUF build that was measured with its quantization and file size, and its 30-day downloads on Hugging Face. With a hardware id every row also carries the fit verdict for that machine at 8K context. Ranked by downloads only; no row says a version is better than its original. Image and video versions are not included.

model.description: Only versions of one tracked model, by slug, e.g. qwen3-8-27b. Slugs come from trending_models.

hardware.description: Hardware id, e.g. rtx-3060-12gb: adds the fit verdict per version. Ids come from list_hardware.

count.description: How many identical graphics cards (default 1). Their memory adds up; the answer says what that assumes.

memory_gb.description: For a machine that is not on the list, instead of hardware: the memory of one graphics card, or of the Mac, in GB.

type.description: What memory_gb describes: "gpu" (default, a plug-in card) or "mac" (unified memory).

ram_gb.description: System RAM behind the card(s), for what spills over (default 32).

tools.name: media_models
tools.description: Tracked open image and video generation models with their measured files. Each model comes in loadouts (for example a 4-bit and a full-precision set of transformer, text encoder and VAE); every loadout gives the sum of its files and its largest single file in GB, measured from the Hugging Face file listing. With a hardware id every model carries a fit verdict for that machine, judged on the largest file held at once against usable memory, for the largest loadout that runs. No runtime peak is computed and there are no speed figures.

family.description: Only image or only video models. Both without it.

hardware.description: Hardware id, e.g. rtx-3060-12gb: adds the fit verdict per model. Ids come from list_hardware.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: What changed, in one call: popularity and GPU rental price moves since the previous day's reading (each item names both readings and their times), models new on the radar, community versions first measured in the last days, and the current pick of the week. Built from stored readings only; it describes what happened and is not a forecast.

days.description: How many days back to look for new community versions (default 7).

tools.name: gpu_prices
tools.description: Rental prices per GPU-hour (USD) for eight GPU classes, per named source, eleven sources in all. Vast.ai: the median of verified on-demand offers with min/p75 and offer counts, the collection timestamp and the Rent Index (this week's median against last week and against the first week collected, a trend word, the days excluded as marketplace glitches). Clore.ai: the median for the same class, a second marketplace kept apart from the first. RunPod: its lowest posted on-demand price (a list price, not a median). AWS, Azure, Oracle Cloud, Lambda, Nebius, CoreWeave, Hyperstack and Google Cloud: pay-as-you-go list prices, each with the instance type, VM size or shape the price sits in (read four times a day, no statement about capacity). The index describes what prices did; it is not a forecast.

tools.name: price_history
tools.description: Daily price history per GPU class and source, up to 365 days (the series starts 26 August 2026): the rows the Rent Index and the 30-day range are computed from. Marketplace days (Vast.ai, Clore.ai) are medians over the day's counted hourly medians with min, p75 and offer count; list-price days (RunPod, AWS, Azure, Oracle Cloud, Lambda, Nebius, CoreWeave, Hyperstack, Google Cloud) carry the posted price. Each row says which kind it is; the two kinds are not comparable. Describes what prices did; it is not a forecast.

gpu.description: One class by slug or name, e.g. rtx-4090, h100. Every class without it.

source.description: One source key, e.g. vast, runpod, aws. Every published source without it.

days.description: Days back from today (default 30, max 365; the series starts 26 August 2026).

tools.name: list_hardware
tools.description: Curated GPU and Mac profiles the fit engine knows — ids, memory, usable memory after margins, bandwidth. The ids are what find_fit takes as hardware.

tools.name: weekly_pick
tools.description: The current pick of the week: one tracked model chosen by a published rule (largest counted Heat Score rise among models that run comfortably on a consumer card of up to 24 GB), with the numbers frozen at selection time, a device-by-device fit ladder and the written report including its caveats. Pass week (e.g. 2026-w37) for a past issue. issue is null until the first issue is published.

week.description: ISO week label of a past issue, e.g. 2026-w37 (default: the current issue).
